description: The counter at a county or town office: the clerk greeting the next person, handing over and checking a form, taking a fee and giving a receipt, asking for an ID, answering a question, and closing; and the person at the counter asking. Every part is a whole sentence said or written in public-domain records (federal hearings and briefings, Election Assistance Commission and Federal Election Commission meetings and guides, federal counter guides, Florida's election and county offices), with record words as slots. A clerk at a counter is rarely recorded, so one public-domain record from 2015 on is enough for this bank.

slots.fee: A fee from the office's fee records.
slots.payee: Who a check is made out to, from the office record.
slots.time: An opening or closing time, from the office's hours.
slots.body: Another office, from the office records.
slots.place: A place, from the place records.

mining.rule: A shape is kept when at least 1 documents say it as a whole sentence and one of them is a public-domain record from 2015 or later, which is its source.
